description:
Found in defk-9p6.13 (cosine_topk.exs), trying a dimension-major index (scores += column * q[d], one axpy per dimension). Repro (report: :full):

  defk axpy(m :: [f32], s :: f64) :: [f64] do
    out = alloc(f64, len(m))
    for i <- 0..(len(m) - 1)//1 do
      out[i] = out[i] + m[i] * s
    end
    out
  end

Both bounds checks are dropped, but the report says 'non-finite: float checks raise where they fail: the body's state cannot be restored from a snapshot to replay a strip' and 'not vectorised: Cannot vectorize early exit loop with writes to memory'. A flagged strip would need to undo the strip's writes to out (or snapshot the strip's slice of out) before replaying with raising checks. The dimension-major cosine scan (100k x 384, in place into a 100k-element f64 score array) ran ~26 ms, no faster than the row-major dot with 8 partial sums (20 ms), which does vectorise via SLP. The same read-modify-write shape is matmul's i-k-j inner loop (out[i * p + j] = out[i * p + j] + aik * b[k * p + j]) and any histogram/accumulator update; worth checking whether matmul is held back by it.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Experiment: let a flagged strip that writes elements of an array it also reads (out[i] = out[i] + x[i] * c) snapshot the strip's slice and restore it before replaying with raising checks, so read-modify-write float loops can vectorise

**Current behavior:**

    defk axpy(m :: [f32], s :: f64) :: [f64] do
      out = alloc(f64, len(m))
      for i <- 0..(len(m) - 1)//1 do
        out[i] = out[i] + m[i] * s
      end
      out
    end

drops both bounds checks, but the report says "non-finite: float checks raise where they fail: the body's state cannot be restored from a snapshot to replay a strip" and clang does not vectorise ("early exit loop with writes to memory"). The same shape is matmul's i-k-j inner loop and accumulator/histogram updates. Dimension-major cosine scan ran ~26 ms vs 20 ms for the vectorised row-major dot.

**Desired behavior:**
- A flagged strip whose body writes to an array may run flagged when the written elements in the strip are a contiguous slice it can save before the strip (bounded size: the strip length) and restore before the raising replay, so the observable result and raised error are exactly those of the checked form.
- Applies only where the write set is provably the strip's slice (index = loop counter plus a fixed offset, one array); everything else stays as today.
- The flagged-strip memory-safety and replay argument in the runtime header is updated (this builds on defk-5qk's update).
- Measure axpy, matmul's i-k-j loop and the dimension-major cosine scan; adopt only if a measured win, otherwise record and leave it.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] axpy runs flagged and vectorises (report: :full) if adopted; timings before/after in docs/performance.md
- [ ] Tests: a NaN/inf produced mid-strip raises the same error with the same out contents as the checked form (agreement), including the first and last element of a strip and under forced yields
- [ ] Non-matching shapes (two written arrays, a gather write out[idx[i]]) stay as today
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Bounds-proof changes (defk-2mz); writes to more than one array per strip

Built the slice snapshot (sr_slice: every write of the array a proven store at the loop counter or counter + strip-invariant value; the strip saves [idx at first trip, idx at last trip] in a DEFK_STRIP-element stack buffer before it runs and restores it before the replay). axpy and friends then run flagged and clang vectorises them (width 4, interleave 4). Measured best of 15, load 5-6, main vs branch: axpy f32->f64 4096 x976 1.99 -> 2.47 ms, 65536 2.80 -> 2.99, 1M 1.44 -> 1.58, 4M 1.49 -> 1.63 (+5..24%); axpy2 (f64, 2 passes) 2.72 -> 3.24, 3.37 -> 3.63, 1.60 -> 1.85, 1.74 -> 1.93; in-place passes out[i] = out[i]*s + 1: 4096 1.04 -> 0.95 (-9%), 65536 1.07 -> 1.25, 1M 1.19 -> 1.38; accum out[i] += b[i]*b[i]: 2.25 -> 3.13 (+39%, and clang still does not vectorise it: 'cannot identify array bounds', two double* arrays); cubic out[i] = x*s + x*x*(1-x)*0.25 + 0.125: 4096 2.53 -> 1.61 (-36%), 65536 2.43 -> 1.91 (-21%), 1M 2.63 -> 1.97 (-25%). The 16 KB memcpy per strip is 8 B per element of extra traffic: memory-bound bodies (2 float ops) lose, compute-bound ones (6 ops) win. matmul's i-k-j loop and the dimension-major cosine scan cannot use it anyway: their write/read indices (i*p+j, base+r) keep bounds checks (defk-pvt), so the writes are checked puts, not proven stores. Not adopted: no unconditional win. Code reverted; numbers go to docs/performance.md. Option for a follow-up decision: adopt the slice only when the body has >= 4 flagged float ops per element (cubic yes, axpy/accum no), or an explicit per-loop opt-in.

PR #27 opened (docs record only): https://github.com/DanielLuning/defk/pull/27. The slice snapshot is not adopted; a heuristic (>= 4 float ops per element) or a per-loop opt-in is the owner's call. Ticket stays in progress until the merge.

title: In-place accumulate out[r] = out[r] + x[i] * c keeps per-operation float checks, so an axpy loop does not vectorise
